:::{#exm-cauchy-sequence}
#### A Cauchy sequence of real numbers

The [real numbers](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/number-systems.html#def-real-numbers) $\reals$ with the [inner product](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-inner-product) $\iprod{x}{y} = x\,y$
form an [inner product space](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-inner-product-space),
and $\norm{x} = \abs{x}$ in it.
The [sequence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-sequence) $x_n = \frac{1}{n}$ is a [Cauchy sequence](#def-cauchy-sequence).
Given $\tolout > 0$,
take $N$ to be any [natural number](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/number-systems.html#def-natural-numbers) larger than $\frac{1}{\tolout}$.
[For all](proof-writing.qmd#def-universal-quantifier) $m, n \ge N$,
both $\frac{1}{m}$ and $\frac{1}{n}$ lie in $(0, \frac{1}{N}]$,
so $\abs{\frac{1}{m} - \frac{1}{n}} < \frac{1}{N} < \tolout$.
For example, with $\tolout = 0.01$,
take $N = 101$:
all $m, n \ge 101$ have $\abs{\frac{1}{m} - \frac{1}{n}} < \frac{1}{101} < 0.01$.
